rules.statement: In a civil case, if an objection has not been taken at the closure of the case of the opposite party that the documents marked subject to proof were not proved and therefore be rejected, they become evidence for all intents and purposes without the requirement of further proof despite the subject to proof objection taken at the time of marking the said documents.
rules.supporting_quote: it is well settled law that, in a civil case, if an objection has not been taken at the closure of the case of the opposite party that the documents marked subject to proof were not proved and therefore be rejected, they become evidence for all intents and purposes without the requirement of further proof despite the subject to proof objection taken at the time of marking the said documents.
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: section 154A (3) of the Civil Procedure Code as amended by the Act No. 17 of 2022
